label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=7), stronger with length
explanation: Fires almost exclusively (97% of mass) at the delimiter step (input <DEL>, about to output the first original token) and only when the sequence is long: ~90% of <DEL> steps for L=7, ~100% for L=8 and 9, ~2% for L=6, never for L<=5. Magnitude grows with L: L=9 delimiters carry ~47% of mass, L=8 ~37%, L=7 ~13%, and top activations (~4.1) are all L=9. Weaker secondary firing (~2.7% of mass, ~0.3-0.4 of max) on the last original token of L=9 sequences (t=8), i.e. the step just before <DEL>, which the predicate omits. Never fires in the copy phase or on earlier original tokens; token identity (out_tok, first_tok, prev tokens) barely modulates it.

issues: The claims hold up on the test split. The predicate (phase==1)&(L>=7) scores P=0.967, R=0.884, F1=0.924, mass recall 0.972, matching the reported numbers.
Dev profile: 97.3% of activation mass is at the delimiter step, 2.7% is on original tokens and 0% is in the copy phase (0 of 2.73M copy steps active).

Firing rate on <DEL> steps by length (test): L=7 precision 0.90, L=8 0.99996, L=9 1.0, L=6 under 0.1%. On dev, L<=5 never fires. Magnitude grows with L: in the top activation quartile, 74% are L=9 delimiters and 26% are L=8.

Misses (2.8% of mass) are mostly the claimed L=9, t=8 last-original-token firing (36% rate, about 0.02-0.17 of max), plus 38 activations at orig_idx 7. The explanation discloses this. Adding it to the predicate gives F1 0.896, so the original predicate is the better one.
False positives (8243) are L=7 delimiters where the feature stays off, about 10% of them. These are the known soft threshold at L=7; no token pattern stood out in the sampled sequences.
Minor: the label says 'stronger with length' without noting the small secondary firing at L=9 t=8, but the explanation covers it.
